Subject: Operational runbook & attestation stub for no-training (draft)

Hi Sarah — attaching a draft attestation and the subprocessor manifest we can share (attached). Below is a concise operational summary we'll expand in the pack: 

- No-training enforcement: a per-tenant flag disables upstream model update pipelines and blocks any internal model-improvement queues. Configuration is enforced at the request-router and persisted in tenant config. We will include a config snippet showing the flag set to "disabled" for your tenant ID.

- Data flow & retention: interaction data is written to a short-term ingestion queue, optionally mirrored to an encrypted SFTP export. Default interaction log retention for no-train tenants is 0 days for model pipelines (i.e., not forwarded to training queues) and 30 days for audit logs (configurable). We'll provide a sample audit-log with anonymized request-ids.

- Subprocessors: the attached manifest enumerates the inference runtime, telemetry pipeline (audit store), and storage provider. We include vendor contact and country. Any subcontractor with access to raw interaction text is marked and accompanied by a contractual restriction.

- Key management & residency: we support tenant-scoped KMS keys (customer-managed) and onshore-only routing in our US region. We'll include KMS key IDs and the HSM attestation status in the pack.

- Ownership/derivatives: Redwood's standard proposal for no-train customers is explicit: customers retain output ownership; Redwood will not claim derivative rights, and we will add this to the attestation language. We'll provide suggested DPA wording for your team to redline.

Attachments in this message: attestation-stub.pdf (draft), subprocessor-manifest.csv

- Sarah: confirm if audit-log anonymized snippet is sufficient (we will redact user identifiers).
- Insight legal: share any specific redline language you require beyond the template.
- Redwood: we will upload the full evidence pack and a 30-minute walkthrough recording by 2026-08-26.
